chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: God Mighty and Majestic says to the angel assigned to the believer when he falls ill: 'Write for him what you used to write for him during his good health, for it is I who have placed him in My bonds (of illness).'

key_terms.الْمَلَكُ الْمُوَكَّلُ: The assigned/allocated angel — in Islamic cosmology, every believer is attended by recording angels who document their deeds
key_terms.حِبَالِي: My bonds/ropes — metaphor for illness as divine binding, implying gentle custody by God
key_terms.صِحَّتِهِ: His good health — the baseline period against which the sick person's deeds are measured

ai.seo_question: Does a sick Muslim receive reward for good deeds they cannot perform due to illness?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a divine statement (hadith qudsi) reported by Imam al-Sadiq on the authority of the Prophet. God commands the recording angel to continue crediting a sick believer with all the good deeds they performed in health, since God Himself has caused the illness. The phrase 'My bonds' (حِبَالِي) conveys that illness is God's gentle captivity — keeping the believer from action while ensuring no spiritual reward is lost. This reflects the Shia theological emphasis on divine justice (adl) and mercy: God does not penalize the believer for a condition He ordained.
